title: Canonical request envelope + OTEL span linker for structured-log ingestion
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Introduce a lightweight, backwards-compatible 'request_envelope' structure and an OTEL-aware span-linker enrichment stage in the ingest pipeline so that structured logs, traces, and metrics can be reliably joined for latency/error dashboards and root-cause analysis.

Background: We currently have many formats arriving at the telemetry ingress (JSON lines, plaintext, legacy app logs). Correlating logs with traces is brittle: some services emit trace IDs, others do not. Downstream dashboards (Console latency heatmaps, SLO error breakdown) require a deterministic way to surface all events belonging to a logical request.

Scope:
- Define canonical request_envelope schema (JSON) that contains: request_id, trace_id (optional), span_id (optional), service_context (service_name, env, version), route_context (route/path, http_method), timing hints (start_ts, end_ts optional), payload_refs (pointer to raw log or structured fields), and provenance (forwarder_id, ingestion_node).
- Add an enrichment stage to the ingress pipeline (otelcol/fluent-bit layer) called envelope-assembler that:
  - Parses incoming event, extracts existing trace/span fields if present.
  - Runs deterministic request_id generation heuristics when trace_id missing (stable hashing of session/user/request headers + timestamp bucket).
  - Emits the event with request_envelope as top-level field and preserves original payload under payload.raw.
- Implement an OTEL span-linker component in the Loki/ELK pipeline that:
  - Joins events to OpenTelemetry traces using trace_id/span_id when available.
  - Falls back to request_id to group log lines across services.
  - Emits metadata tags used by Console (tenant, route, latency_bucket).
- Schema enforcement and lightweight validation in the ingest gateway to reject or tag malformed envelopes.
- Canary rollout plan: enable envelope-assembler for 10% of synthetic traffic and 3 pilot tenants, monitor ingress CPU, event p99 latency, and false-positive grouping rate.

Performance targets and trade-offs:
- Aim for <0.5ms additional latency per event in the ingress path at 95th percentile; keep added memory overhead minimal by streaming transformation (avoid materializing large buffers).
- Trade-off: deterministic request_id heuristics may group unrelated events in extreme edge cases; provide conservative sampling and a 'relax_match' flag for pilot tenants.

Migration:
- Backfill script to annotate historical logs with best-effort request_ids for a 30-day retention window (offline job).
- Expose a Console migration view that shows percent of logs with request_envelope present by service.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingested events (canary tenants) include request_envelope with correct fields > 99% of the time for structured inputs.
- Console latency page can 1) group traces+logs by request_id and 2) show error-rate per-route using envelope metadata.
- CPU overhead on ingress fleet < 8% at production QPS during canary.

Stakeholders: Runtime infra (Marcus Li), Console (Sofia Romero), Observability SRE (Evan Thompson), SDK/Forwarders (Jules Martin).

Artifacts: Detailed design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/OBS-req-envelope, implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2476, benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/envelope-bench
comments: 2025-01-09 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after SRE postmortem; initial design sketch added to Confluence. Asked Runtime infra to evaluate runtime cost baseline.

2025-01-10 - Marcus Li: Reviewed design; proposed moving deterministic request_id generator into the forwarder to reduce cross-node reconciliation. Raised concern about increased cardinality in Loki labels—suggest using request_id as an index field, not a label by default.
2025-01-11 - Sofia Romero: Console team confirmed required envelope fields for dashboard joins. Requested inclusion of route_context.http_method and service_version to support regression rollups.

2025-01-12 - Marcus Li: Spike results attached in PR 2476 show 0.35ms median and 0.62ms p95 per-event added latency using otelcol processor with streaming parser. Memory overhead acceptable in 2GB worker tests.

2025-01-13 - Evan Thompson: SRE recommends conservative default: envelope assembled only for JSON inputs, and plaintext pipelines should be tagged for future rollout. Added requirement for per-tenant feature flag and metric emit (envelope.assembled.count).

2025-01-14 - Implementation: initial envelope-assembler code landed behind feature flag in platform repo (PR 2476). Integration tests added (unit + e2e synthetic trace/log join). Preparing canary rollout for 3 tenants next week.

2025-01-15 - Review notes: Design reviewer Jules Martin asked to add TTL on request_id to avoid unbounded label growth when storing as index. Action: change storage to keep request_id as dedicated index column in Loki v2 mapping; follow-up ENG ticket planned.
